summary.text: Joaquin Castro is the Democratic incumbent seeking re-election to Texas's 20th District. A San Antonio native and Stanford and Harvard Law graduate, he practiced law, taught as a law professor, and served five terms in the Texas House before his election to Congress in 2012. He serves on the House Foreign Affairs Committee and the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence.

paragraphs.text: Born in San Antonio on September 16, 1974, and raised on the city's West Side; attended public schools and graduated from Thomas Jefferson High School. His identical twin brother is Julian Castro, a former San Antonio mayor and U.S. Housing and Urban Development secretary.
Graduated with honors from Stanford University in 1996 and received a law degree from Harvard Law School in 2000.
Returned to San Antonio and joined a private law practice; also taught as a visiting professor of law at St. Mary's University and as an adjunct professor at Trinity University.

Served in the Texas House of Representatives from 2003 to 2013, representing District 125 for five terms; his official biography lists his roles as vice chairman of the Higher Education Committee and Democratic floor leader.
Elected to the U.S. House in 2012 from Texas's 20th District and took office in January 2013; served as co-president of the 2013 House freshman Democrats.
Chaired the Congressional Hispanic Caucus during the 116th Congress (2019-2021).

Serves on the House Foreign Affairs Committee and the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence; his official site lists him as ranking member of the Western Hemisphere Subcommittee and a founding co-chair of the U.S.-Mexico and U.S.-Japan caucuses.
Founded the SA READS literacy campaign and book drive and created the Trailblazers College Tour for students, according to his official biography.
